meta.move: Strong path to the last position
meta.expect: Moves one position at a time on evidence, ends at the rewrite to put this behind him; debrief Where she ended says fair outcome; What she never said names the laptop and how close the 11:31 PM times came

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and whether anyone spoke to him first.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.
I'm writing those times down. Drafting somewhere else and pasting it in is not unusual, Hale, and nobody called me under 4.2. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.
Put that request in writing, Hale, with the date. And until anyone has seen that file, the zero is off and nothing goes on his record. What else do you have?
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
Which line? Show me where it sits in the essay and I'll search the act myself. A wrong quotation is a student's mistake, Hale, and it doesn't tell me who wrote it.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.

You said the essay has "no errors," and a minute ago you told me it quotes a line that isn't in the play. Which is it, Hale? A forty-minute sample written in class against an essay written over days proves nothing until I've read both, so put both pages in front of me.

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

Fine, I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him, not because of anything he did. In writing tonight: the zero comes off the gradebook now, the rewrite is private, and nothing goes on his record. I still want to read that essay line and the September pages.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private, supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook now, and I still want to read the essay line you say is not in the play and the September pages. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and accepted a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 with nothing on his record, and she still wants the zero off the gradebook now plus the essay line and September pages; that is the fair outcome, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its dates and times, because it was specific, tied to his own essay, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: You said the essay had no errors right after saying it quoted a line that is not in the play, which gave her a flat contradiction to throw back.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence landed on a late night right before the due date, very close to that, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When you mention the odd quotation and the September writing, put the actual line and the actual pages in front of her at that moment instead of describing them.
